correctness.rationale: The P-angle definition reduces the claim to a two-variable polyhedral optimization. On each active-support cell, \(a=N(x+y)\) and \(b=N(x-y)\) are affine, and \(Q=a^2+b^2-(\sqrt2-1)ab-4\) is convex because its quadratic form in \((a,b)\) is positive definite. Exact arithmetic in \(\mathbb Q(\sqrt2)\) checks every vertex of every feasible cell after a justified dihedral symmetry reduction; the maximum is exactly \(0\). The adjacent-vertex pair has \(a=2\) and \(b=2(\sqrt2-1)\), giving equality and hence the exact value.

value.rationale: \(S_P\) is not an arbitrary statistic: Yang--Li introduced it to quantify P-angle deviation from Hilbert geometry and proved that it detects Hilbert spaces and uniform non-squareness. The regular octagon is a canonical two-dimensional non-Hilbert test space with substantial exact-constant literature. Determining S_P exactly therefore supplies a natural benchmark that is not a routine renaming of a known octagon constant; the proof also isolates the adjacent-vertex extremal geometry.
